hero.title: Law in Sweden for Indian Students
paras: **Law in Sweden** offers opportunities for students interested in international law, human rights, commercial law, investment arbitration, intellectual property and legal research. Swedish universities provide different study pathways, including professional law programmes and specialised postgraduate degrees.

highlights.title: World-Class Nordic Innovation
highlights.desc: Study in Sweden's globally ranked universities renowned for pioneering scientific breakthroughs, design thinking, and sustainable research.

highlights.title: English-Taught Degrees
highlights.desc: Over 1,000 bachelor's and master's degree programs delivered entirely in English with international accreditation.

highlights.title: Generous Post-Study Work
highlights.desc: Sweden offers residence permits after graduation for students to seek employment or start innovative businesses.

highlights.title: High Quality of Life
highlights.desc: Ranked among the top nations globally for safety, equality, environmental sustainability, and student well-being.

overview: However, students should understand an important distinction: most Swedish law degrees that prepare graduates for domestic legal practice are taught in Swedish, while several specialised master's programmes are available in English.

For Indian students, the right pathway depends on their career goals. Those who wish to practise law in Sweden must understand the Swedish language requirements and professional qualification process. Students interested in international legal careers may consider an English-taught LL.M. after completing a recognised law degree.
Through Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad guidance, students can explore suitable universities, understand admission requirements and compare the available **law courses in Sweden**.

universities.name: \. Uppsala University
universities.desc: Uppsala University offers a professional Law Programme worth 270 credits, normally completed over 4.5 years. The programme is taught in Swedish, so applicants must meet the required Swedish-language proficiency. ![][image1] The university also offers the **Master's Programme in Investment Treaty Arbitration**, an English-taught postgraduate programme for eligible law graduates. It focuses on international investment law and the resolution of investment disputes.

universities.name: \. Stockholm University
universities.desc: Stockholm University offers specialised English-taught master's programmes, including: * LL.M. in International Commercial Arbitration Law * LL.M. in European Intellectual Property Law ![][image2] These programmes are designed for students with a qualifying legal education who want to develop specialist knowledge in international commercial disputes or intellectual property law.

universities.name: \. Swedish Defence University
universities.desc: The Swedish Defence University offers a one-year **Master's Programme in International Operational Law**. It covers international law relating to armed conflict, military operations, human rights and peace operations. Applicants must hold a relevant legal qualification and satisfy the programme-specific academic and admission requirements. ![][image3] **Important:** Programme availability, admission criteria, teaching language and tuition fees can change. Always confirm the latest information through the official university programme pages.

items.q: Can Indian students apply for Law in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, Indian students with qualifying credentials meeting English language proficiency (IELTS/TOEFL) and academic prerequisites can apply to recognized universities in Sweden.

items.q: What is the medium of instruction for Law in Sweden?
items.a: Most master's and international bachelor's degree programmes are taught entirely in English for international students across Swedish universities.

items.q: What are the typical tuition fees for Law in Sweden?
items.a: Tuition fees for international students generally range between SEK 80,000 and SEK 150,000 per year, depending on the institution and level of study.

items.q: Can international students work while studying in Sweden?
items.a: Yes, non-EU international students holding a valid Swedish residence permit for higher education are permitted to work alongside their studies without a fixed hours limitation during term time.
